questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_L02_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.C.01

Which oral outline order is strongest?

answer.text: A. Closing, evidence, random fact, opening, claim.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This order is confusing.

answer.text: B. Opening, claim, evidence, reasoning, closing.

feedback.text: Correct. This order gives listeners a clear path.

answer.text: C. Evidence only with no claim.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Evidence needs a claim and reasoning.

answer.text: D. Random facts with no closing.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is not organized oral communication.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_L02_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.W.02

What is a claim?

answer.text: A. A source title only.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A title is not a claim.

answer.text: B. A random number from a survey.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A number may be evidence, not the claim.

answer.text: C. A closing thank-you only.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That may end a presentation, but it is not a claim.

answer.text: D. The main point the speaker wants the audience to accept or understand.

feedback.text: Correct. A claim states the speaker's main point.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_L02_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.RS.01

Which evidence is most credible?

answer.text: A. A survey of 120 students reports that 68 remain on campus after dismissal at least one day each week.

feedback.text: Correct. This is specific source-based evidence.

answer.text: B. Someone said it is true.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague and unsupported.

answer.text: C. I feel like students wait around.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is personal opinion.

answer.text: D. Everybody knows the answer.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is not credible evidence.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_L02_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.W.02

Which sentence gives reasoning?

answer.text: A. Source A surveyed students.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is source information, not reasoning.

answer.text: B. Source B is from a handbook.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This identifies a source.

answer.text: C. This matters because students who already remain on campus need a safer and more productive supervised location.

feedback.text: Correct. This explains why the evidence supports the claim.

answer.text: D. The survey number is 120.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is evidence detail.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_L02_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.R.06

What central idea connects Source A and Source B?

answer.text: A. Students remain on campus after dismissal, and supervised locations matter.

feedback.text: Correct. This idea reflects both the survey and handbook.

answer.text: B. Students should block hallways.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The handbook says students should not block hallways.

answer.text: C. Surveys are not useful.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Source A provides useful survey information.

answer.text: D. No students stay after school.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Source A says many students remain on campus.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_L02_Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.C.01

Which opening best prepares listeners for the topic?

answer.text: A. I have random facts.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague and weak.

answer.text: B. This is about stuff after school.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague.

answer.text: C. I do not know what this is about.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not prepare listeners.

answer.text: D. Today I will explain why a supervised after-school study space would help students who remain on campus.

feedback.text: Correct. This opening identifies the topic and purpose.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_L02_Q07

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.RS.01

Why is the handbook excerpt useful evidence?

answer.text: A. It is unrelated to school procedures.

feedback.text: Incorrect. It is directly related to school procedures.

answer.text: B. It states an expectation that students should wait in supervised locations.

feedback.text: Correct. This directly supports the need for a supervised space.

answer.text: C. It is only a personal opinion.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A handbook excerpt is an official school source.

answer.text: D. It proves students never wait after school.

feedback.text: Incorrect. It does not say that.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_L02_Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.W.02

Which pair correctly labels evidence and reasoning?

answer.text: A. Evidence: This matters because students need safety. Reasoning: 49 students wait in hallways.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The labels are reversed.

answer.text: B. Evidence: I think it is good. Reasoning: survey.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague and mislabeled.

answer.text: C. Evidence: 49 surveyed students wait in hallways or similar areas. Reasoning: This shows a supervised study space would address an existing need.

feedback.text: Correct. The evidence gives source information, and reasoning explains it.

answer.text: D. Evidence: random thoughts. Reasoning: source name.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is not accurate.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_L02_Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.C.01

Which closing statement is strongest?

answer.text: A. That is it.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is weak and undeveloped.

answer.text: B. I am done talking.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not reinforce the presentation.

answer.text: C. The survey was a survey.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is repetitive and weak.

answer.text: D. A supervised study space would turn after-school waiting time into safer and more productive academic time.

feedback.text: Correct. This reinforces the claim and reasoning.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_L02_Q10

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.R.06

Which statement best identifies a central idea?

answer.text: A. Supervised after-school locations matter because many students remain on campus after dismissal.

feedback.text: Correct. This is a complete central idea.

answer.text: B. The source has numbers.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too vague.

answer.text: C. The handbook is a book.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is not the central idea.

answer.text: D. A bus loop exists.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This detail is not the central idea.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_L02_Q11

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.RS.01

Which evidence should a speaker avoid using as the main support?

answer.text: A. Student survey data with a stated sample size.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is credible evidence.

answer.text: B. An official school handbook excerpt.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is credible evidence.

answer.text: C. A vague statement that "everybody says so."

feedback.text: Correct. This is not credible or specific.

answer.text: D. A specific number from a relevant survey.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This can be credible evidence.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_L02_Q12

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.C.01

Which transition would best introduce evidence?

answer.text: A. In conclusion

feedback.text: Incorrect. This signals a closing, not evidence.

answer.text: B. According to Source A

feedback.text: Correct. This clearly introduces source-based evidence.

answer.text: C. Anyway

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is informal and weak.

answer.text: D. Randomly

feedback.text: Incorrect. This weakens organization.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_L02_Q13

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.W.02

Which sentence combines claim and reason clearly?

answer.text: A. The school should create a supervised study space because many students remain on campus after dismissal.

feedback.text: Correct. This states a claim and a reason.

answer.text: B. Study space, students, after school, survey.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is not a complete claim.

answer.text: C. The handbook is there.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague.

answer.text: D. I want a room.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is personal and lacks reasoning.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_L02_Q14

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.C.01

What makes oral organization different from simply listing facts?

answer.text: A. Oral organization avoids all evidence.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Strong organization uses evidence.

answer.text: B. Oral organization means speaking as fast as possible.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Speed does not create organization.

answer.text: C. Oral organization means using no closing.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A closing helps listeners remember the point.

answer.text: D. Oral organization connects facts in a sequence that listeners can follow.

feedback.text: Correct. Organization helps listeners understand how ideas connect.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_L02_Q15

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.RS.01

Which detail from Source A best supports the claim that many students remain on campus?

answer.text: A. The source is called Student Survey Summary.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The title does not prove the number of students.

answer.text: B. Some students have opinions.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague.

answer.text: C. 68 of 120 surveyed students reported remaining on campus at least one day each week after dismissal.

feedback.text: Correct. This detail directly supports the claim.

answer.text: D. The handbook has rules.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is from Source B and does not give the survey count.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_L02_Q16

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.W.02

Which reasoning sentence best explains Source B?

answer.text: A. The handbook exists.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not explain why the evidence matters.

answer.text: B. Because the handbook expects supervised waiting locations, a study space would help students follow school procedures.

feedback.text: Correct. This explains how the evidence supports the claim.

answer.text: C. The handbook has pages.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is irrelevant.

answer.text: D. Source B is a source.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is circular and not reasoning.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_L02_Q17

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.C.01

Which speaking note is clearest?

answer.text: A. Stuff: after school maybe.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague.

answer.text: B. Say something about halls.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is not a clear speaking note.

answer.text: C. Claim: The school should provide a supervised after-school study space.

feedback.text: Correct. This note is clear and labeled.

answer.text: D. Talk random source.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is unclear.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_L02_Q18

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.R.06

Which source detail develops the central idea that supervision matters?

answer.text: A. The handbook says students should wait in supervised locations.

feedback.text: Correct. This directly develops the idea that supervision matters.

answer.text: B. The survey includes 120 students.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This supports student presence more than supervision.

answer.text: C. Students completed a survey.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not focus on supervision.

answer.text: D. The bus loop exists.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not develop the supervision idea.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_L02_Q19

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.C.01

Which problem would hurt an oral presentation most?

answer.text: A. Using a clear opening.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A clear opening helps.

answer.text: B. Jumping from claim to unrelated facts with no reasoning.

feedback.text: Correct. This would make the message hard to follow.

answer.text: C. Explaining evidence.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Explanation helps.

answer.text: D. Ending with a closing statement.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A closing helps listeners.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_L02_Q20

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.W.02

Which item is evidence, not reasoning?

answer.text: A. This matters because students need safe spaces.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This explains importance, so it is reasoning.

answer.text: B. Therefore, the claim is stronger.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is reasoning language.

answer.text: C. This shows the need is real.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is reasoning.

answer.text: D. Source A reports that 49 students usually wait in hallways or similar areas.

feedback.text: Correct. This is a source-based fact, so it is evidence.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_L02_Q21

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.C.01

Which checklist best matches Lesson 2?

answer.text: A. Claim, credible evidence, reasoning, logical order, closing.

feedback.text: Correct. This is the Lesson 2 organization process.

answer.text: B. Random facts, no claim, no order, no closing.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This weakens oral communication.

answer.text: C. Opinion only, no evidence, no explanation.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Credible evidence is required.

answer.text: D. Closing first, then unrelated source details.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This order is confusing.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_L02_Q22

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.RS.01

Why is a specific survey number stronger than "many people say"?

answer.text: A. Specific numbers are always fiction.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The survey number is source-based.

answer.text: B. Vague wording is always more credible.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Vague wording is weaker.

answer.text: C. Specific numbers give concrete evidence that listeners can evaluate.

feedback.text: Correct. Concrete evidence is stronger than vague claims.

answer.text: D. Evidence should never be specific.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Specific evidence is usually stronger.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_L02_Q23

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.R.06

Which sentence best summarizes Source A?

answer.text: A. No students remain on campus.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Source A says many students remain on campus.

answer.text: B. All students leave immediately.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This contradicts Source A.

answer.text: C. The handbook lists supervised locations.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That describes Source B.

answer.text: D. A student survey found that many students remain on campus after dismissal, and many wait in informal areas.

feedback.text: Correct. This accurately summarizes Source A.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_L02_Q24

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.C.01

Which oral note best introduces reasoning?

answer.text: A. Source A says 49 students wait in hallways.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This introduces evidence.

answer.text: B. This evidence matters because it shows the school already has students who need an organized waiting location.

feedback.text: Correct. This introduces reasoning.

answer.text: C. The survey counted students.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is evidence.

answer.text: D. The handbook has a rule.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is evidence.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U06_L02_Q25

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG2.W.02

Which final statement best connects claim, evidence, and reasoning?

answer.text: A. Since survey data and handbook expectations both show a need for supervised locations, a study space would support student safety and learning after school.

feedback.text: Correct. This connects sources, claim, and reasoning.

answer.text: B. The source set is over now.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not connect the ideas.

answer.text: C. Students and handbooks are things.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague and not logical.

answer.text: D. I listed facts, so no explanation is needed.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Evidence needs reasoning.
